Below is what I could verify from each organization’s **official giving / grants pages** (or, for the donor-advised funds, their nonprofit/granting pages), including **application deadlines/cycles** when they’re publicly posted, plus the **key “what you’ll need” items** that usually trip people up.

> Quick reality check: a lot of “big brand” foundations are **invitation-only** most of the time. When that’s the case, there is **no public deadline** because you can’t submit a cold application. I noted those clearly.

## Corporate foundations and major corporate programs

| Funder | Official program page | Application deadline / cycle | What you need to apply (or to get considered) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Walmart Local Community Grants (Spark Good Local Grants)** | Spark Good Local Grants guidelines citeturn0search20turn0search0 | **Quarterly windows** (dates posted by year; example cycles shown on Walmart guidelines). citeturn0search0 | Apply through Walmart’s portal; typical basics: **501(c)(3) / public entity eligibility**, org info, project description + budget, compliance items; note org application limits per year/quarter in guidelines. citeturn0search0 |
| **Target Community Giving (Target Circle partner program)** | Target Circle Community Giving page citeturn0search5 | **No single universal deadline shown** (applications open/close depending on program cycle/market). citeturn0search5 | This is not a traditional “submit anytime grant.” You apply to be considered as a Target Circle nonprofit partner; expect program-specific requirements and review timelines. citeturn0search5turn0search1 |
| **Target Foundation (general grants)** | Target Foundation overview / how grants work citeturn0search21 | **Mostly invitation-only**. citeturn0search21 | Practical takeaway: to get funded you usually need alignment + relationship/partner channel (or be in a specific open program like Target Circle). citeturn0search21turn0search5 |
| **Amazon Community Impact Grants** (no single universal program page) | Amazon community impact overview (programs vary by region/theme) citeturn4search5 | **Varies by specific program** (many are regional funds or topic-specific open calls). citeturn4search5 | You’ll typically need to find the *specific* Amazon fund/open call relevant to your geography or cause (examples include AWS Imagine Grant, local community funds run with community foundations, etc.). citeturn4search5turn0search6turn4search21 |
| **AWS Imagine Grant (Amazon)** | AWS Imagine Grant + FAQ (timeline posted by cycle) citeturn0search2turn0search6 | **Annual cycle**; deadlines are posted each year (example: Round One and Round Two dates shown for a prior cycle). citeturn0search6 | Nonprofit eligibility, proposal narrative, plus whatever the year’s RFP/instructions require; sign up for alerts when the next cycle opens. citeturn4search1turn0search6 |
| **The Home Depot Foundation (grants hub)** | Home Depot grants landing page + required docs page citeturn0search3turn0search15 | **Program-dependent** (Veteran Housing, Retool Your School, etc. run on their own timelines). citeturn0search3 | Home Depot explicitly lists **required attachments/templates** (budget template, board template, reporting templates, etc.). citeturn0search15 |
| **Verizon Foundation (general grants)** | Verizon grant requirements page citeturn1search12 | **Invitation-only** for new applications. citeturn1search12 | You generally need to be invited; align to stated priority areas and build the relationship path. citeturn1search12 |
| **Comcast NBCUniversal Foundation (NBCUniversal Local Impact Grants)** | Local Impact Grants site + Comcast press release (dates posted by year) citeturn6search2turn1search5 | **Annual window** (example: March–April window shown for 2025; site often shows “applications closed” when shut). citeturn1search5turn6search2 | Eligibility constraints (expense range, markets served, etc.) and typical nonprofit financial docs (their FAQ mentions 990 requirements in some years). citeturn6search14turn6search2 |
| **Citi Foundation** | Citi Foundation “Apply for Funding” + example RFP PDF with deadline citeturn1search2turn1search6 | **RFP-based**: deadlines depend on each open RFP. citeturn1search2turn1search6 | You apply to specific RFPs; expect eligibility screens, narrative, budget, and portal submission tied to the RFP instructions. citeturn1search2turn1search6 |
| **PepsiCo Foundation** | PepsiCo Foundation overview page citeturn1search15 | **Varies** (often scholarships/programs; not one universal open grant deadline). citeturn1search15 | Best practice: treat as program-specific. When you find a relevant program, follow that program’s posted requirements and dates. citeturn1search15 |
| **The Coca-Cola Foundation** | Coca-Cola Foundation page (grant proposals policy) citeturn3search0 | **No public deadline** because they **do not accept unsolicited grant proposals**. citeturn3search0 | You generally cannot submit a cold grant. Use their partner pathways/portals if available and build relationship/partner alignment. citeturn3search0 |
| **AT&T Foundation** | AT&T giving portal citeturn2search1 | **Invitation-only**. citeturn2search1 | No public deadline; you need to be invited. citeturn2search1 |
| **Google.org** (grants) | Google.org open calls vary; example open call site citeturn6search7 | **Program-specific** (open calls publish their own deadlines). citeturn6search7 | Watch for “open call / accelerator” postings; each has its own eligibility, narrative prompts, and timeline. citeturn6search7 |
| **Google for Nonprofits (incl. Google Ad Grants)** | Eligibility page citeturn2search2turn6search23 | **No deadline** (it’s an eligibility + activation process, not a one-time grant round). citeturn2search2 | You’ll need nonprofit verification and to meet Google’s eligibility rules (and category exclusions). citeturn2search2 |
| **Salesforce Foundation (strategic grants)** | Salesforce Foundation page (unsolicited proposals) citeturn2search3 | **Invitation-only** for strategic grants. citeturn2search3 | No cold applications; relationship/partner channels matter. citeturn2search3 |
| **Johnson & Johnson (grants & giving – J&J Innovative Medicine)** | J&J grants & giving landing page + guidelines citeturn3search1turn3search17 | **Depends on the specific grant type** (educational/medical/patient org grants each have processes). citeturn3search1 | Expect portal registration and structured requirements (requestor registration, authorized signer, and program guidelines). citeturn3search17 |
| **CVS Health Foundation** | CVS Health Foundation grants page citeturn3search2 | **Invitation-only** for foundation grants. citeturn3search2 | Common “open-ish” pathway is **employee-driven** programs like Volunteer Challenge Grants (if you have a CVS colleague championing). citeturn3search18turn3search2 |
| **UnitedHealth Group / United Health Foundation** | UHF grant seeker info citeturn4search0 | **Invitation-only**. citeturn4search0 | You must receive an invitation; then you’ll submit via their process with standard nonprofit documentation. citeturn4search0 |
| **Pfizer Foundation (competitive grants / RFPs)** | Pfizer competitive grants page + example RFP PDF citeturn3search3turn3search7 | **RFP-based**: deadlines posted inside each RFP. citeturn3search3turn3search7 | Watch the RFP listings; each one sets timelines, required content, and submission steps. citeturn3search3turn3search7 |

---

## Donor-advised funds (Fidelity / Vanguard / Schwab / National Philanthropic Trust)

These are **not corporate grant programs you apply to**. They’re **DAF sponsors**. The donor recommends a grant to your nonprofit; the sponsor approves and sends funds.

| Organization | Official nonprofit / granting info | Deadlines | What you should do to “be ready” |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Fidelity Charitable** | Recommending a grant (process) citeturn4search10 | **No deadlines** (donors grant anytime). citeturn4search10 | Make sure your org is in good standing + easy to verify; have correct legal name/EIN, mailing address, and a receipting contact ready. citeturn4search10 |
| **Vanguard Charitable** | Nonprofits info page citeturn5search7 | **No deadlines**. citeturn5search7 | Same readiness checklist: EIN/legal name match, address, and fast response if they request verification. citeturn5search7 |
| **Schwab Charitable (DAFgiving360)** | How to recommend a grant (explains grant letter/check flow) citeturn6search0 | **No deadlines**. citeturn6search0 | Be easy to vet; keep your nonprofit records clean so grants don’t stall. citeturn6search0turn6search4 |
| **National Philanthropic Trust (NPT)** | NPT “For Nonprofits” + Grant Payments PDF citeturn6search5turn6search1 | **No deadlines**. citeturn6search5 | Big tip: register for **PayPal Grant Payments** to receive funds electronically faster (optional but helpful). citeturn6search5turn6search1 |

---

## Bank foundations (Wells Fargo / JPMorgan Chase / PNC / Capital One)

| Funder | Official giving / grant process page | Application deadline / cycle | What you need |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wells Fargo Foundation** | Wells Fargo grant process page citeturn4search3 | **Invitation code required** to apply in portal; if not invited, you can submit an **interest form** (no posted deadline). citeturn4search3 | Be ready for outcomes reporting requirements and alignment to their focus areas; portal access is invitation-code driven. citeturn4search3 |
| **JPMorgan Chase Foundation** | J.P. Morgan foundations online application “foundation finder” tool citeturn5search0 | **Varies by program/foundation** (many opportunities are program-specific). citeturn5search0 | Use their tool to identify the right foundation/opportunity for your geography; then follow that specific program’s requirements. citeturn5search0 |
| **PNC Foundation** | PNC Foundation page + (for some programs) guidelines PDF citeturn5search1turn5search17 | **Program-specific** (some initiatives have their own process and documentation expectations). citeturn5search17 | Expect a structured application (often via CyberGrants) and documentation around need, program plan, and metrics depending on initiative. citeturn5search17 |
| **Capital One Foundation** | Capital One community page (grant requests) citeturn5search18 | **Invitation-only** for typical grant requests; sometimes they run **open calls/RFPs**. citeturn5search18 | If you see an open call, follow its posted deadlines; otherwise this is relationship-driven and not a cold-apply situation. citeturn5search18turn5search6 |

---

## What you typically need for almost any funding application

Even when the funder’s portal questions differ, most ask for the same core pieces:

- **Organization identity:** legal name, EIN, address, website, leadership contact
- **Proof of status:** IRS determination letter (or government affirmation letter for public entities)
- **Financials:** latest Form 990 (or audited statements), current-year budget, sometimes prior-year revenue/expense totals
- **Governance:** board list (sometimes with affiliations), conflicts policy (sometimes)
- **Project plan:** problem, solution, timeline, target population, geography served
- **Outcomes + measurement:** specific metrics you’ll report (outputs + outcomes)
- **Budget for the ask:** project budget, what you’re requesting, how funds will be used
- **Compliance attestations:** nondiscrimination, lobbying limitations, etc. (varies)

If you tell me **what you are applying for funding for** (your mission + geography + whether you’re a 501(c)(3) or for-profit), I can:
- flag which of the above are **actually open-apply** vs invitation-only for your situation
- and give you a prioritized shortlist of the best-fit opportunities from your list (plus what to prepare first).
